title: paged KV cache: optimize block allocator, reuse and pinning to reduce GC pressure and improve tail latency
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Improve paged KV cache block manager: compact allocator, block reuse, pinning API; reduces GC churn and improves tail latency for long-running chat and streaming workloads.
description:
Context: Recent production incidents and bench runs showed elevated CPU time spent scanning and compacting KV cache blocks, and higher latency tail when workloads produced many short-lived prefixes. This PR refactors the paged KV cache block manager to introduce a compact, freelist-based block allocator, stronger reuse heuristics, and an explicit pinning API for hot KV blocks.

Motivation: reduce GC-like traversal costs, avoid accidental eviction of hot prefixes, and make reuse deterministic under high concurrency.

Design & changes:
1) block_allocator: replace bump/bitmap allocator with compact freelist allocator that segregates small/medium/large blocks and supports lock-free (per-shard) free lists where possible; allocate-on-demand and reuse buckets to reduce zeroing costs.
2) reuse heuristics: add LRU-ish per-shard reuse windows and a reuse_promote() path invoked on cache hits to bias reuse for hot prefixes.
3) pinning API: expose pin_block(block_id) / unpin_block(block_id) for the serving runtime to avoid eviction of blocks that are currently being streamed or used by long KV cache pinned contexts. Pinning increments a pin counter; eviction skips pinned blocks.
4) background compaction: lightweight compaction task now runs with backoff and will not preempt hot shards; it is cooperative and yields to the serving scheduler to avoid bursty CPU.
5) metrics & tracing: added kv_cache.block_allocations, kv_cache.block_reuse_hits, kv_cache.block_pins, and kv_cache.compactions{started,duration_ms}.
6) tests & benchmarks: add integration test that simulates interleaved streaming and short-prefix workloads and microbenchmarks for allocation/reuse latency.

Compatibility & migration notes: The pinning API is additive and opt-in from the serving runtime. Default behavior preserved for existing workloads. The new allocator changes in-memory layout but is compatible with persisted snapshots; an upgrade path is included in paged_block_manager's load path for rolling upgrades (it will migrate pages lazily).

Benchmarks & impact: On perf-canary we observed:
- 28% reduction in median allocation latency for hot-path allocations
- 35% reduction in CPU time spent in block scanning/compaction
- 12% improvement in 99.9th percentile tail latency for interleaved streaming workloads
- KV cache memory overhead steady; reuse reduces churn

Impact & follow-ups:
- Short-term: monitor kv_cache.block_reuse_hits and block_pins in production dashboards; tune reuse windows.
- Medium-term: consider exposing pinning to SDK-level controls for customers that want to mark prefixes sticky.
- Follow-up PR planned to make compaction scheduler-aware and plumb a global knob for debug eviction.

Related work: PRs pr-18742 and pr-19510 contain earlier paged KV cache experiments and incremental allocator changes.
